blocks.text: When we go shopping for food for the family we can find everything we need in a supermarket. There, we serve ourselves, loading groceries from the shelves into a push cart, pushing it up and down the aisles.

The supermarket has an amazing variety of food to select from, such as fresh fruits and vegetables, fish, dairy products, flour, sugar, rice, a large bakery section, meat of all kinds, food for pets, candies, spices, cereals, canned food and a large section of packed frozen foods. Besides food, the supermarket sells cleaning powders and soaps of all kinds, paper, napkins and towels and many household items.

Many foods are completely prepared. These are frozen pizza pies, canned or frozen stews, spaghetti and meat or macaroni and cheese dinners, all pre-cooked. The famous «T.V. Dinners» are very popular because they are cooked while the family is supposedly watching T.V. and will continue watching T.V. as they eat right from the aluminum cooking trays.

items: – Well, hello Angie. What can I do for you today?
– I want to bake a cake for my mother. It’s her birthday tomorrow. I need some ingredients.
– Ummm… a pound will do and, I also want a dozen brown eggs. Please, be sure there aren’t any bad ones. Otherwise, I’ll bring them back.
– Of course, we sell only fresh food here. What else do you want?
– I hardly have any flour. Please, give me some self-raising flour and half a gallon of milk.
– Yes. How much flour do you want?
– Two pounds and er… a pound of butter as well. Oh!, I also need a large bar of semi-sweet chocolate.
– We have a special sale on this new brand of butter. It’s only $1.75.
– All right, I’ll try it out. Do you have any oranges? If they are firm and ripe, I’d like to take some for juice. How much do they cost?
– I’ll get half a dozen, then … O.K. … I guess that’s all. How much is everything, Mr. Jenkins?
– Here you are. Thank you very much, Mr. Jenkins.
– Bye, Angie. Wish your mother a happy birthday.
